The core insight of GenMove is that trajectory tasks—generation, recovery, prediction—can be unified under a masked conditional diffusion framework. This relies on embedding mobility into a dense vector space where temporal masking strategies (random, terminal, sequential, etc.) encode task-specific structure. The model uses a noise predictor trained on noisy embeddings to reconstruct clean trajectories. Contextual embeddings from historical data allow zero-shot transfer. In GSE, this translates to generating rare plays, recovering missing tracking frames, and simulating counterfactuals. The failure mode arises when masks do not align with task semantics or when user embeddings fail to generalize. The isomorphism lies in treating all trajectory tasks as denoising problems in a shared latent space. Dualities emerge between recovery and generation through symmetric masking. The model's robustness hinges on the assumption that mobility patterns are consistent across tasks and users.
